Astellas ASP0367 Primary Mitochondrial Myopathy CONFIDENTIAL ISN/Protocol 0367-CL-1201 ## Conclusions: This CSR presents the results from the phase 2 study, 0367-CL-1201. ASP0367 did not show efficacy over placebo. The study was terminated after interim analysis results showed that the futility criteria were met. - The 0367-CL-1201 study was terminated early following an interim analysis. This analysis, conducted after the predefined, approximately 30 participants completed the primary endpoint assessment at week 24, showed that the study met the futility criteria for the primary endpoint, indicating it was unlikely to demonstrate a positive effect. The interim analysis included data from the first 33 participants who either completed the efficacy evaluation at week 24 or discontinued before reaching week 24. - The primary endpoint (i.e., 6MWT) did not appear to trend or show response to ASP0367 in either dose arm (30 mg, 75 mg). Variability at baseline and at subsequent visits for 6MWT was quite high. - For the primary efficacy endpoint, the LS mean difference (90% CI) in 6MWT results between ASP0367 30 mg and placebo was 9.4 (-28.9, 47.7) m and between ASP0367 75 mg and placebo was -0.9 (-39.8, 38.1) m. - There were no significant trends in the secondary endpoints in ASP0367 any dose group when examined in aggregate. An evaluation of 5XSTS, MFIS, Neuro-QOL SF-Fatigue, Neuro-QOL SF-Mobility, PGIC and PGIS, did not indicate evidence of treatment effect. Responder analyses for the PGIC score at week 24 showed similar positive effects in the ASP0367 30 mg and placebo arms, with 5 participants in each arm categorized as responders, compared to 3 responders in the ASP0367 75 mg group. - Final efficacy analysis was performed in the FAS to assess primary and secondary endpoints. The high variability of results in all treatment arms, evidenced by the large SD or SE, limits data interpretation. The futility criteria were met at the time of the interim analysis and the final results were consistent with the findings of the interim analysis. - A total of 21 randomized participants in the DB treatment period and 6 in the OLE treatment period discontinued treatment. The most common reason for treatment withdrawal was due to a partial clinical hold imposed by the FDA. - The safety and tolerability findings of ASP0367 relative to placebo in the SAF included: - TEAEs were reported in 95.7% of participants in ASP0367 arms in the DB and DB-OLE treatment periods, 100% of participants in placebo arm in the DB treatment period and 100% of participants in placebo to ASP0367 arm in the DB-OLE treatment period. Many of the observed TEAEs were consistent with the underlying disease of PMM. - Serious TEAEs were experienced by 3 participants on any dose of ASP0367 in the DB treatment period of the study and by 1 participant in the OLE treatment period of the study. Of these, 1 was attributed to the study drug. - During the study, 2 participants died: 1 in the DB treatment period and another in the OLE treatment period; both participants had been randomized to treatment with 30 mg of ASP0367. The SAE of death reported for the participant in the DB treatment period was assessed by the investigator as related to study drug. This participant also had AEs of rhinovirus infection, blood CPK increased, and aspiration reported within 8 days prior to the event of death. The fatal SAE reported during the OLE treatment period was ‘suspected cardiac arrhythmias’ and assessed by the investigator as not related to study drug. - Following both single and multiple dosing, plasma exposure to ASP0367 increased proportionally with the dose, although there was high inter-individual variability. The study aimed to evaluate safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy in individuals living with Duchenne aged 8 to 16 years old. The study was stopped early, in November 2022, because not enough patients were available to take part in the study. While the study’s small sample size limits the data interpretation, the results indicate that ASP0367 is safe and well-tolerated. Additionally, for the key efficacy endpoints, the ASP0367 treatment group showed a clinically relevant improvement in parameters compared with those observed in the placebo treatment group. To learn more about the results of the study please see the Plain Language Summary linked in the community letter. Astellas has indicated that they look forward to continuing to work with patients and families to develop new therapies for patients. Based on the positive gene expression data in this study, continued clinical development and evaluation of ASP0367 in the target populations of patients with diseases involving primary or secondary mitochondrial dysfunction are warranted. The objectives of this first‐in‐human trial were to evaluate the safety/tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of ASP0367 in healthy participants. ### Methods In this double‐blind phase 1 study, adult participants were randomized to single or multiple ascending oral doses of ASP0367 or placebo. The study duration was 1 and 14 days, respectively. Pharmacokinetic parameters under fed conditions were also evaluated. ### Results A total of 64 (single‐dose cohort) and 37 (multiple‐dose cohort) participants were included in the study. After single doses of 1 to 120 mg, ASP0367 was rapidly absorbed, with median time to maximum plasma concentration (t_{max}) of 1.50 to 2.24 hours under fasting conditions; ASP0367 concentrations declined in a multiphasic manner after reaching maximum plasma concentration. Under fed conditions, t_{max} was delayed 1.7 hours. After multiple once‐daily doses, mean half‐life of ASP0367 10 to 75 mg ranged from 14.1 to 17.5 hours; steady state was reached after 4 days. Clinical effects of ASP0367 are also of interest in mitochondrial disorders, such as PMM, which similarly have no curative treatments and can also affect skeletal muscle and cause muscle weakness.[ref-type: bibr] ^{27} , [ref-type: bibr] ^{28} In preclinical studies, ASP0367 increased mRNA expression and protein levels of PPARδ target genes in mdx mice and human DMD myotubes (data on file). In three separate studies, once‐daily ASP0367 treatment for up to 35 days increased the exercise endurance of mdx mice relative to the performance seen with mdx mice given vehicle (data on file). ASP0367‐mediated activation of PPARδ in mouse cells as well as human healthy and DMD muscle cells increased FAO (data on file), indicating preliminary amelioration of one key aspect of mitochondrial dysfunction. The aims of this first‐in‐human study were to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of single and multiple ascending oral doses of ASP0367 in healthy adults. ### Safety and tolerability No participants discontinued treatment during part 1. In part 2, two participants randomized to placebo discontinued treatment and withdrew from the study; one of the participants was replaced. In both parts 1 and 2, all treatment‐emergent AEs (TEAEs) were considered mild to moderate in severity. No clinically relevant dose‐ or treatment‐related trends in AEs were observed and no dose‐limiting safety findings were reported. No TEAE was determined to be study drug‐related. No deaths, serious AEs, or TEAEs leading to withdrawal of treatment occurred in this study. In part 1, of the participants who received ASP0367, three reported medical device site reactions (dermatitis due to electrocardiogram [ECG] leads) and one participant each reported vessel puncture site pain, constipation, an arthropod bite, pain in the extremity, and headache. No TEAEs were reported with the ASP0367 60‐ and 120‐mg doses. All AEs in the placebo group were also medical device site reactions arising from dermatitis due to ECG leads. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Astellas Pharma Inc.
